chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Sabbah al-Hazza', from Qutham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Inform me about zakat — how did it come to be twenty-five from every thousand, not less or more? What is its rationale?'

So he said: 'Verily, God, Mighty and Majestic, created all of creation and knew their young and their old, their rich and their poor. So He made twenty-five poor people out of every thousand human beings. And had He known that would be insufficient for them, He would have increased it for them, because He is their Creator and He is most knowing of them.'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: may I be sacrificed for you: a form of devotional address to the Imam expressing reverence and submission
key_terms.زَكَاةِ: zakat: the obligatory annual alms-tax in Islam, calculated as 2.5% of qualifying wealth held for a lunar year
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic: an honorific epithet for God emphasizing His power and transcendence
key_terms.مِسْكِيناً: miskeen (poor/needy person): one of the eight categories of zakat recipients mentioned in Quran 9:60
key_terms.وَجْهُهَا: its rationale/basis: literally 'its face', meaning the underlying wisdom or justification

ai.seo_question: Why is zakat set at 25 per thousand (2.5%) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: A student of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) asks about the divine wisdom behind zakat being set at 2.5% (25 per 1000). The Imam responds that God, in His omniscience, created all humanity and knew precisely the proportion of poor among them — approximately 25 per thousand — and therefore fixed zakat at that rate. The hadith situates the zakat rate within divine providence and God's comprehensive knowledge of His creation's needs.
word_analysis: He would have increased it for them
